_README: Thread C ticker banking recorder -- production configuration.
Editing this file is an operational change, not a code change. Every accepted
change to collection_end_utc is appended to <archive_dir>/config_changes.jsonl.
NO VALUE HERE IS null ANY MORE. Both of the values that were deliberately
left unsupplied have now been supplied from measurement rather than guessed:
disk_reserve_bytes from the Branch-2 capacity hour, and the discovery cadence
from the operational decision recorded below. The recorder still fails closed
at startup if either is removed.
_collection_end_utc: The frozen collection end. Initial value derived from MLB's published
postseason schedule as of 2026-09-03: collection continues through the fifth
calendar day after the latest published postseason game date.
This value may be moved LATER by an operator if MLB's published latest
postseason date moves later. It may NEVER move earlier -- the recorder
enforces that against <archive_dir>/collection_end.state.json and refuses to
start if this file asks for an earlier end.
The recorder does not fetch, parse or monitor the MLB schedule.
_disk_reserve_bytes: SUPPLIED FROM MEASUREMENT. The production reserve is frozen as
R = max(10 GiB, 48 x B_1h), where B_1h is the bytes the filesystem consumed
over one bracketed high-activity hour. THE RUN HAS NOW HAPPENED.
The B_1h used here is the BRANCH-2 measurement -- the ticker-only capacity
hour, which reported B_1h,disk = 267,526,144 bytes/hour. That is the branch
this configuration collects on, so it is the branch the reserve is sized
against. 48 x 267,526,144 = 12,841,254,912, which is above the 10 GiB floor,
It is NOT recomputed from any other hour. The Branch-1 hour (ticker+trade,
373,444,608 bytes/hour) measured a different channel selection and is not
what runs here; a later, busier or quieter hour is not the measurement the
formula was frozen against. Changing R means running the bracketed hour
again and saying which run the new number came from.
10737418240 (10 GiB) is the floor the recorder enforces, not a default.
_discovery_daily_target_utc: RESOLVED. Frozen Rule 1 full-universe discovery runs ONCE PER UTC CALENDAR
DAY, targeted at this wall-clock UTC time.
Why a daily wall-clock target rather than an interval from process start:
an interval measured from startup shifts a little on every restart and
drifts permanently after a few, so a reboot would silently move the cadence.
Anchoring to a UTC time means a reboot at 03:00 changes nothing.
09:00 UTC is chosen as an operational quiet hour: it is 05:00 ET, after the
previous evening's MLB games have settled and hours before the earliest
first pitch, so a ~25-minute, ~13,800-request sweep competes with live
book traffic as little as the schedule allows. The sweep runs on a worker
thread and never interrupts recording either way.
If the recorder was down at the target, that day's sweep runs ONCE as soon
as live recording is restored. The catch-up is inherently today-only: a
discovery census is a snapshot of what the exchange says now and cannot be
taken retroactively for a day already past.
Only a COMPLETE census accepts the UTC day. An INCOMPLETE one leaves the day
unaccepted so it is retried -- the one case where more than one sweep runs
for a day, and the explicit retry the frozen rule allows.
Not configurable and NOT here: discovery_attempt_min_interval_seconds is
FROZEN at 3600 in threadc.frozen. No sweep may start within an hour of the
previous attempt's START, however that attempt ended, enforced against a
timestamp persisted in <archive_dir>/discovery_schedule.state.json and
written before the sweep begins -- so Restart=always cannot turn a crash
mid-sweep into a fresh sweep every RestartSec.
_ws_shards: Number of WebSocket connections the universe is deterministically hashed
across: shard = sha256(ticker)[:16] % ws_shards. Kalshi publishes an error
code for 'subscription market limit exceeded' (26) but no number for the
limit, and the recorder will not bisect against the server to find one. Raise
this if a shard exceeds max_markets_per_shard or if the server ever returns
code 26; changing it re-partitions the universe and every moved market is
_channels: WHICH CHANNELS PRODUCTION BANKS. This key may only ever name a non-empty
SUBSET of the frozen pair in threadc.frozen.CHANNELS -- it can subtract,
never add. Removing the key restores the frozen pair; adding a channel that
is not in it is refused at startup, because widening what the bank preserves
changes the fidelity boundary and the storage schema and is a code change.
BRANCH 2 OF THE PRECOMMITTED FALLBACK HIERARCHY: ticker only.
Both branches were measured over the same bracketed hour, the same universe
and the same storage schema. Branch 1 (ticker+trade) reported
267,526,144 bytes/hour. Branch 1 does not fit the 137 GB free for the
collection window, so collection proceeds on Branch 2 fidelity.
THIS KEY IS WRITTEN EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN LEFT OUT. Absence means the frozen
pair, which is Branch 1 -- the branch the measurement rejected. A production
start with no channels key would therefore silently revert to it.
What this costs is recorded in research/THREADC_FIDELITY_BOUNDARY_V1.md:
the archive keeps the displayed state at the touch and loses every public
print. The selection is written into the startup record, the readiness line,
the ws_session rows and the OPEN and final manifests, so no segment can be
read later as a two-channel segment in which nothing happened to trade.
_max_markets_per_shard: Occupancy above which a shard is reported over capacity. 0 disables the
check. Reported, never auto-fixed: the recorder does not re-partition itself.
